Only 13 of the 140 are disambiguated by grade alone. The other 127 need a second discriminator, and picking one means ruling on which item IS the canonical breakthrough pill and what the other two are - an item-identity decision, not a rename.
next: Wave 72 fixes the deterministic subset: the 1 chain-stages group and the 13 grade-unique groups, using the grade prefix that 5322 of 7273 existing names already follow. Leave the 46 benign material groups alone. The remaining 127 need an explicit ruling first: decide the canonical item per colliding name, then either rename the losers to reflect what they actually are or delete them as duplicates. Do not delegate that ruling to content-generation agents - they will improvise inconsistent discriminators.

title: ADR 0025 migration left tools/data.py blind to every modifier - audit clean is meaningless and authored stat-set diversity was erased
source: wave 72 verification after the ADR 0025 corpus migration landed mid-wave
reason: ADR 0025 Accepted 2026-10-02 replaced ItemDef stub flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers with fixed_modifiers holding a master option id plus value, and a roll_spec, then migrated the corpus. 7950 of 7950 item files now carry fixed_modifiers and roll_spec and zero carry the old maps. Three consequences. First, the gate is blind - tools/data.py line 44 still declares dicts as flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers only, and every audit and distribution rule reads those two keys, so the audit sees zero modifiers corpus-wide and reports data audit clean while validating nothing, and tools data distribution prints Modifier Stat Distribution none plus 34 declared stats never used by any item, which is false since it is all 34. A clean audit is no longer evidence of anything. Second, authored diversity was destroyed rather than migrated - a wave-72 five-stat item authored as breakthrough_chance plus evasion plus fortune plus penetration plus physique at three-decimal percents now reads fixed_modifiers with a single base_comprehension option at integer value 6 and roll_spec count 1, so the stat-combination and modifier-value diversity built across waves 69 to 72, including 100 percent stat-pair coverage, 142 distinct three-stat sets and 81 distinct percent values, is no longer present in the data. Third, tools/data.py still emits the dead schema, since _new_command writes percent_modifiers and flat_modifiers, so any item created with data new --percent lands in the legacy shape while the corpus is in the new one. HEAD item_def.gd still accepts both shapes through build_fixed_modifiers, which is why 4849 of 4890 tests pass. tools/item_migrate.py, the tool that rewrote all 7950 files, is still untracked.
next: Do not dispatch item-generation agents until tools/data.py is taught the ADR 0025 schema: add fixed_modifiers and roll_spec to the parsed dicts, rewrite every modifier rule to read them, and either teach _new_command to emit fixed_modifiers and roll_spec or document that new items are still authored in the legacy shape. Until then do not cite data audit clean as evidence, and treat the tools data distribution modifier sections as non-functional. Separately decide whether the authored stat-set programme is retired under ADR 0025 - if it is, waves 69 to 72 need a target expressed in option-pool membership, roll budget and rarity/realm pairing rather than authored stat combinations.

title: ADR 0025 catalog eligibility is category-scoped and far too narrow - 99.4 percent of authored stat diversity was silently discarded on migration
source: wave 72 survival measurement against the ADR 0025 catalog
reason: ADR 0025 replaces authored stat maps with master-catalog option references, and the catalog is far narrower than the stat vocabulary the corpus uses, so authored diversity is discarded rather than migrated. Measured over wave 72 own 344 non-material items: of 501 stat tokens encoded in their ids, only 3 survive as fixed_modifiers options, a 0.6 percent survival rate. Per item, 242 lost every authored stat, 101 lost some, and 1 kept all. The cause is category-scoped eligibility. The catalog holds 107 options over 92 stats, but eligibility is narrow and unequal: equipment gets 93 options over 92 stats, technique gets 36, material gets 5, and consumable gets only 9 - awareness, body_integrity, desire, essence, health, mind_power, qi, stamina and tribulation_essence. Those 9 consumable options are resource pools, not combat stats, so a consumable item can no longer carry a combat modifier at all. Every one of the 184 consumable items in this wave now grants health via the restore_health category default instead of its authored effect. tools/item_migrate.py drops any stat whose option is ineligible or missing with no warning, and then substitutes CATEGORY_FIXED, so the loss is silent.
next: Decide the programme target before another wave. Authored stat-combination diversity is void under ADR 0025: pair coverage, three and four and five stat sets, and novel modifier values cannot survive migration for consumable items and mostly cannot for technique items. The expressible axes are now option-pool membership, roll budget where count comes from rarity via RARITY_COUNT common 1 magic 2 rare 3 legendary 4, rarity and realm pairing, and category eligibility coverage. Two things need an owner decision. First, whether consumable items are meant to carry combat stats at all, since the current catalog says they cannot and the corpus says they always did. Second, whether the catalog should be widened so technique and consumable have real option coverage. Until that is settled, target equipment only, where all 92 stats are eligible. Separately, tools/data.py still parses only flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers, so data audit and data distribution cannot see any modifier and a clean audit is not evidence.

title: tools/item_migrate.py is broken and untracked - missing import zlib makes the only sanctioned ADR 0025 migration path unrunnable
source: wave 73 end-to-end schema probe in an isolated temp root
reason: tools/item_migrate.py is the only sanctioned path from authored stat maps to ADR 0025 option references, and it cannot run. Line 164 calls zlib.crc32 inside realm_for, but the module imports only re, pathlib.Path and two local modules - there is no import zlib anywhere in the file. Every run dies on the first item with NameError: name zlib is not defined, confirmed against an isolated temp root and against the real corpus with --limit 1. The file is also untracked with no git history at all, so the migration that rewrote all 7950 item files cannot be reproduced from anything in the repository and the working state of the tool is unknown. Consequence: nobody can author new-schema content, and nobody can re-run or verify the corpus migration.
next: Add import zlib to tools/item_migrate.py - that single line is the whole fix, and the tool then runs in dry-run by default so it is safe to validate before --apply. Then commit the tool, because until it is tracked the corpus migration is unreproducible. After that, verify the migration is faithful by re-running it in dry run and confirming it reports zero changes, which also proves the 7950 already-migrated files are stable under it. Only then re-target generation, per DEF-0048.

title: HALF STALE: the mind screen IS built, routed and prices itself by role; what is left is that reward MAGNITUDE has no readout and realm advance fires no signal
reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger). The 'mind screen is still unbuilt' half is FALSE: res://src/ui/screens/mind_cultivation_screen.tscn exists, its script is game/src/ui/screens/mind_cultivation_screen.gd, and it is ROUTED - game/src/app/screen_routes.gd:74-78 registers id &"mind_cultivation" against that scene. The 'costs are not surfaced' half is also FALSE, and was fixed by ADR 0151: the screen renders preview's costs as a Needs line (mind_cultivation_screen.gd:320-334) and names every refusal price by ROLE rather than by id (:403-453), which is the pattern the other screens now copy. What SURVIVES is narrower and is a readout gap, not a build gap. (1) Reward magnitude has no row anywhere: the award is authored per realm (all 30 mind seeds carry {will: 2.0}, a flat value - see BL-0115) and the screen shows the sea, the gates and the costs but never what a breakthrough PAYS, so a player cannot see that the payoff does not scale. (2) A realm advance is not surfaced: core/actor.gd:8 emits path_advanced at core/breakthrough.gd:47 and it still has ZERO listeners, so nothing on any screen reacts to a breakthrough landing - which is also the surviving half of DEF-0078.

(1) Publish the award in preview's cost-adjacent shape (advancement.gd:464-466 already reads seed.rewards) and render it beside the Needs line, so the payoff is visible even while it is flat by design - that is what turns BL-0115's balance ruling into something a player can judge rather than something only a test can see. (2) Attach one listener to path_advanced so a breakthrough is observable; DEF-0078 records that this is the same item and names core/actor.gd:8 and core/breakthrough.gd:47. Do NOT re-file this entry as 'the mind screen is unbuilt' - that claim is three commits stale and any agent who trusts it will rebuild a screen that exists.

title: Realm rewards are a flat constant on every realm seed - a balance decision, not missing mechanics
reason: qi grants {spirit: 2.0} and mind {will: 2.0} on all 30 realms each, against a now-measured power ladder of P=1.00 to 601.43 (ADR 0016). The mechanic is correct and transactional - the award is granted exactly once per resolved attempt and survives save/load - but the magnitude is unauthored, so a R1 pill and a R30 pill grant the same amount. This is a tuning decision about how reward should scale, not an unfinished feature.
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL, and the qi half of it is measured identically to the mind half, which is useful: a reader who thinks one path retuned and the other did not has not looked at both. qi grants {spirit: 2.0} and mind grants {will: 2.0} - I re-measured all 30 files under game/data/mind_cultivation/realms/ and the set of distinct values has cardinality 1, so mind's flat award is not a mind quirk, it is the shared shape. The mechanic is correct and transactional (the award lands exactly once per resolved attempt at advancement.gd:464-466 and survives save/load), so this stays a tuning decision. THE PART THAT MAKES IT ACTIONABLE: the magnitude is ALSO unasserted on both paths, so a retune is invisible to the suite - and the reason is a tautology rather than a gap. game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:239 asserts will == before + _award(seed) where _award at :108-112 sums the same seed.rewards dictionary the code awards from, so any retune satisfies the assertion by construction; nothing pins 2.0. Assert the magnitude against a number the TEST owns before ruling on it, or the ruling is unfalsifiable. If the owner rules that rewards scale, the scale to read is the authored per-realm multiplier in core/realm_power_table.tres keyed by realm id - NOT a computed curve - and rewards stay flat-by-default until then; do NOT reintroduce the removed shared power ladder (ADR 0050 deleted it). Do not write a generator-parity assertion instead: tools/cultivation/seed_systems.py writes the same 2.0, so parity is satisfied by any value the generator and the seeds agree on. Cross-references: BL-0115 (the mind half), BL-0164 (the mind assertion gap), BL-0153 (the adjacent mind balance question, which gate should price the ladder).

title: The shipped save persists items only; realm, progress, meridians, acupoints, sea and loot are dropped
source: CLOSED 2026-10-04 by RE-MEASUREMENT (session mind-ledger). The premise - only items persist - is false. SaveApi.persist is called from PRODUCTION at game/src/app/item_workbench_play.gd:161 and :179 (SaveApi.persist(_actor, DifficultyApi.current_id(_actor))), and SaveApi.restore is called at game/src/app/item_workbench_app.gd:336. save/api.gd:61 builds the payload with actor.to_dict(), so realm, progress, meridians, acupoints, the sea and every module ledger ride the actor's own schema rather than an items-only side file. The module is not an empty facade either: twelve static functions including install_store/store_for (the ADR 0128 world envelope), publish_world, world_state and _snapshot_world/_live_envelope. MEASURED PROOF THAT THE CULTIVATION STATE ACTUALLY SURVIVES, which is what the old items-only claim could not show: game/tests/modules/save/test_cultivation_boot_round_trip.gd:108-120 asserts MindStats.SEA_CAPACITY is present in derived_all() AND greater than zero after a restore, and :190 asserts the same for the restored actor - a published stat that only exists if the sea component, the realm seed and the provider all came back. Note game/src/modules/save/api.gd:23 carries a docblock saying SaveApi.restore() has no caller in res://src outside this file; that line is now STALE against item_workbench_app.gd:336 and is itself a small bookkeeping defect - the docblock is exactly the BL-0619 decay this ledger pass exists to stop. The remaining save questions are DEF-0192's, not this one's: autosave ownership and whether the envelope is complete.

title: Scaled attack and defense stats have no reader, so the 551x ladder is unobservable
reason: RealmScaling.apply has one production caller (core/breakthrough.gd:46) and lands on seven MULT modifiers including ATTACK_PHYSICAL, DEFENSE_SPIRITUAL, DEFENSE_PHYSICAL. SUPERSEDED IN PART by ADR 0124 and by this same entry's own successor work: modules/combat/exchange.gd:118-142 now builds offense/guard bundles from all four attack/defense ids and CombatDamage.resolve_hit (damage.gd:62-105) consumes them in real arithmetic, so the four RealmScaling feeds ARE now readable on the shipped path - ui/screens/loot_encounter.gd:124 calls CombatApi.exchange. Two narrower items survive: (1) Stat.PENETRATION still has no reader in the combat_engine spine - qi_damage.gd:373 reads the different CombatStats.PENETRATION id; (2) the path_advanced signal (core/actor.gd:8, emitted core/breakthrough.gd:47) still has zero listeners, so a realm advance is still not surfaced to the player. next: Attach a listener to path_advanced so the realm ladder is observable in a screen (the readout surface is blocked on DEF-0054 UI), and decide whether Stat.PENETRATION gets a spine reader or is deleted as dead. ADR 0124 carries the corrected census; do not re-derive the 25/13 figures.

title: Body breakthrough roll is pinned at chance_cap from R10 to R30
reason: tools cultivation audit now computes this mechanically instead of trusting the seed fields. Confirmed and quantified: at dao_fruit chance_base 0.75 equals chance_cap 0.75, and from immortal_sovereign upward chance_base EXCEEDS chance_cap (0.76 vs 0.74, 0.77 vs 0.73, 0.77 vs 0.73, 0.78 vs 0.72). title: Technique system: codex, slots and mastery
reason: DONE, re-measured rather than read (BL-0619: a tracked finding decays silently). Every claim this entry made as of 2026-10-03 still holds and the shape has grown: 16 source files (claimed 13), 52 authored .tres, a facade at exactly 12 public methods against the MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS cap of 12, both screens routed through screen_routes.gd, delivery wired through ItemUse._apply_learned to _study_technique, and upkeep settled from StatusLoop.tick. The three ADR 0053 states are distinct and real: a manual delivers (TechniqueCatalog.delivers), the codex owns permanently and unequipping keeps the entry with its rung, and the slot bindings serialise through TechniqueSlots.to_dict with the applied record travelling alongside them (DEF-0152). Ten independent feature-completeness audits found and closed sixteen gaps behind this umbrella; the last four were features built at 90+ assertions that only tests called.
next: None. The umbrella is satisfied; individual gaps live as their own entries.

title: Author TechniqueDef: the schema for a learnable art
reason: A technique has no content type. ADR 0056 settles the layer (module-owned Resource, per the 25-of-30 precedent), but no field list exists. The genre reference supplies the required axes: grade, active-or-passive, element, school, meridian or acupoint gate, qi cost, cooldown, mastery ceiling, and whether the parents are consumed on fusion. None can be invented later without reauthoring every technique.
next: Write the field list with ADR 0055's magnitude ladder and ADR 0054's modifier path as explicit inputs; pin every field with a contract test.

title: Learn a technique: codex entry, path gate and learning cost
reason: ItemUse._apply_learned grants flat base attributes once and discards the item, so all 1363 technique items are interchangeable stat sticks. ADR 0053 requires study to produce a permanent, path-gated CodexEntry instead. The learning cost needs a per-realm ladder whose step stays at or below the authored work budget, or technique study becomes the cheapest power in the game.
next: Implement study consuming the item into a CodexEntry, gate on the technique's own path rank rather than the best path, and size the learning ladder to the measured 1.035714 floor.

title: Three cultivation seeds have drifted from their generators
reason: Because the generators skip existing files, the authored .tres seeds no longer match the code that supposedly defines them. qi.progress_required is authored as 100*max(1,R-1) but seed_systems.py emits 100*max(1,i)^1.45; qi.comprehension_required is authored as 10+2*max(1,i) but the generator emits 10+6i+2i^2; body.work_required corresponds to a power table of roughly 4329x, not the authored 551.46x. A fresh checkout regenerating any of these changes every step ratio, which is exactly what DEF-0083 sizes its ladder against.
next: Reconcile generator and data, then pin the step ratios with a test so the work-budget floor in ADR 0055 cannot silently move.

title: Equip techniques into path-typed slots
reason: ADR 0053 requires per-path slot counts plus universal slots growing with realm tier, so a loadout is a statement about which path is being bet on. The genre convention is four active slots and a known set far larger than that; the gap between known and equipped is the design space. Nothing in the repo expresses a slot limit today.
next: Implement equip/unequip against the codex, with slot counts read from each path's published configuration and universal slots keyed off realm tier.

title: Deliver passive techniques as namespaced StatModifiers
reason: ADR 0054 settles the mechanism. The audit confirmed the cost is about 110 lines in one new file with no change to ActorStats, Equipment or the modifier pipeline, because ItemEffects.stat_modifiers is already a static module-agnostic facade used by sockets and set bonuses. The source tag must be technique:<id> so it cannot collide with the &"realm" tag or an instance id.
next: Copy the SocketEffects.apply shape for rebuild, and wire a settle loop that suspends a technique whose upkeep it cannot pay without unequipping it.

title: ItemRequirement resolves realm to the best path, so path-scoped gates cannot reuse it
reason: item_requirement.gd:140-151 deliberately takes the highest realm ordinal across every cultivation path, documented as so an item never demands one specific system. A qi technique must be gated on the qi rank alone, so the existing scalar min_realm_index cannot express the requirement. This is the only genuinely unavoidable change to a shared item type that the technique system forces.
next: Add a path-scoped ordinal alongside min_realm_index, or gate in the technique module's own validator and leave ItemRequirement untouched.

title: Equipment.rebuild ignores suspension, so rebuilding a suspended slot reactivates it
reason: equipment.gd effects(slot) returns an empty array for a suspended slot, but rebuild() at line 109 reads ItemEffects.resolve directly and would re-add a suspended item's modifiers. The consequence today is latent because nothing in src/ calls settle; it becomes real the moment a tick scheduler drives upkeep. The technique system needs the same pattern to be correct.
next: Add the is_suspended check to rebuild() and pin it with a test that a suspended slot survives a rebuild.

title: Mastery: a per-technique ladder that scales power, cost and cooldown together

title: QiStats.TECHNIQUE_POWER and TECHNIQUE_COST_REDUCTION are provider-only and have no modifier reader
reason: Both stats now have a consumer, and the suite that pins it proves the price is a SINGLE product. technique_casting.qi_cost_for is authored * qi_cost_column * (1 - cost_reduction_of(actor)): the rung discounts the price and never touches the rate, so the two cannot stack. The rate is composed from the published technique_cost_reduction through ActorStats._ensure_providers, PERCENT options composing additively against the cap, and it is CLAMPED before use. Mutation-proved both halves: replacing the product with a sum (qi_cost + rate) turns the suite red on the identity, and removing the clamp drove the price to -119.45, i.e. a cast that pays the actor. The earlier entry said these were provider-only with no reader; that was true on entry and false by the time it was written, so the seven failing assertions were a stale test, not a code defect.

Do not open a picker: ADR 0065 makes destiny earned, never chosen. Decide separately whether the origin grant belongs in app/actor_factory.gd rather than the player root, so every actor that should carry a ledger gets one without relying on the lazy self-attach.

title: Destiny-gated content ships and opens: quests and events both gate on DestinyApi.gate
reason: The original reason said nothing asked the question. It is asked in two places now. QuestApi reads DestinyApi.gate in offered, accept and gates_for, so a quest whose requirement does not pass is never offered and never accepted. EventGate delegates the three fate verbs verbatim to DestinyApi.gate instead of re-implementing them, so there is exactly one fate evaluator in the repo and event cannot become a second one answering a slightly different question. Both consume AUTHORED requirements: the_severed_calling requires has_destiny the_severed AND has_fate oath_breaker, the_returned_instrument requires has_destiny the_one_who_returned, and two events carry a has_fate row. The gate is a used surface, not an unused one.
next: SHIPPED 2026-10-03. Two authoring lessons are recorded so the pattern is copied rather than reinvented. First, keep gating as data: a gated quest or event is a .tres edit, never GDScript. Second, EventGate's local verbs are fact and declare; everything fate-shaped is delegated, so a new fate verb is added to DestinyGate and inherited by both modules at once. No story system exists yet - that part of the original claim is still true - but the quest and event halves are closed.

title: No calendar or period accumulator exists, so fate cannot accrue over calendar time
reason: If a fate ever needs to accrue over time - a counter that rises per day survived, a destiny that unlocks after a season - nothing in this repo can express it. There is no calendar, no period, and no turn boundary; the repo has exactly three frame drivers, all in app/, and no elapsed-time accumulator. DestinyApi.record() is the accrual verb and takes an explicit amount from a caller, so a time-based earn has nothing to convert a duration into. CORRECTED 2026-10-03: this entry previously claimed 'no tick advances time' and that the only ticks are per-frame physics, which was wrong - app/item_workbench_app.gd:98 already owns a single frame driver wired down through app/status_loop.gd:56, and test_status_clock.gd pins the tree to exactly three. The real gap is the absence of a PERIOD, not of a tick.
next: Resolved for destiny: nothing in the destiny module needs calendar time today, and destiny is not expected to own a clock. Whoever needs a period (BL-0198 among them) builds a PERIOD ACCUMULATOR hung off the existing app/ tick - it must add ZERO new frame drivers, because a fourth _process fails game/tests/app/test_status_clock.gd:222-230 - and then calls DestinyApi.record(counter_id, n) per elapsed period. Do not give destiny its own timer: a second time source is a second answer to when a save happened.

title: A consume/clear fate affordance contradicts ADR 0065 and is refused here on purpose
reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 and the row is a REFUSAL, not a gap - which is what it always was, and it is correct to leave standing as a record rather than to 'fix'. It records that a consume/clear fate affordance contradicts ADR 0065 and is refused on purpose. That is still exactly right: fate belongs to the SOUL and is earned and permanent, so a clear verb would let a player erase the record of what they did, and the earn-only invariant is enforced structurally - DestinyApi exposes no remove/revoke/consume verb at all, so the affordance is not merely refused at runtime, it does not EXIST. ADR 0181 then made this load-bearing rather than merely tidy: _carry_destiny moves the whole ledger onto the body a soul re-embodies into, so a consume verb would have a second implementation to keep in sync with the carry.
next: No action, deliberately. Keep this row OPEN as the standing record of a decision someone will eventually try to reverse - a title system or an item that 'clears a curse' is the obvious future request, and the answer is that fate is not a buff to be cleaned off. It is the same shape as ADR 0065's own note that signals live on an instance and not on the facade: the refusal is enforced by the ABSENCE of a verb, which is stronger than a runtime check and cannot be forgotten by a caller who never had the method. If a future mechanic genuinely needs to remove a fate, that is an ADR, not a patch - and it must answer what it means for a soul that has already re-embodied three times.

title: The fate ADR needed a number free of a concurrent collision, and every source citation was repointed
reason: docs/adr/0061-a-tribulation-is-fought-and-its-reward-is-paid-once.md already recorded an unrelated decision, so 0061 was not free. title: Fate category has no closed vocabulary, and data audit reports notes without gating them
reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04: still open, and the vocabulary is now MEASURED rather than guessed. Six categories are authored across the 21 shipped fates - blood (5: ancestral_debt_unpaid, first_blood_duel, household_registered_as_heir, one_hundredth_slain, the_third_man_spared), oath (3: oath_breaker, oath_kept_under_witness, oath_of_the_empty_hand), rebirth (6: debt_carried_forward, reborn_in_a_lesser_vessel, remembered_by_the_mountain, soul_marked_once, soul_marked_thrice, soul_marked_twice), heaven (3), severance (2), debauch (2). No other value appears. The field IS consumed - FateRow._category() renders it in the codex meta line - so it is publish-and-display rather than dead, but nothing GATES it: grep for a fate-category check in tools/data.py returns nothing, so an author may write category = &"tribulation" and the build says nothing while the codex renders a word no other fate carries.
next: SHIPPED as a measurement; the fix is owed and is now fully specified, so it is cheap. Add a FATE_CATEGORIES closed set to FateDef beside the TAGS constant ADR 0189 added - the same shape, the same reasoning (an open vocabulary is an authoring surface that can silently diverge), and the same _tag_findings mechanism already proven in tools/data.py: fail a fate whose category is outside the set, with the six values above as the set. Why a gate and not a warning: unlike a counter with no producer (a dormant row costing one dispatch), a typo'd category is a word the PLAYER reads in the codex, so it is a lie in the one surface meant to be honest. Keep it a separate constant from TAGS on purpose - a tag answers 'what kind of deed' and a category answers 'which story thread', and merging them is the ADR 0066 second-copy failure. Also unmeasured and worth checking when that lands: whether FateRow should ORDER by category, because six flat buckets with no order is the same defect DestinyDef.tier has.

title: a captive is a custody claim, never a tradeable thing
reason: The brief asks for captured actors and mobs to trade. ADR 0094 already refuses it by construction: an Actor has no ItemDef, so base_worth is 0 and exchange hits no_settlement, writing nothing. Making it tradeable needs either a captive ItemDef, which would put a person through RARITY_WEIGHT and RealmRate and assign them a market price, or a second leg type, which is the and-rule and the ADR 0066 failure. The representation is an InstitutionClaim obligation line: transferred moves the claim and settles the old holder's line; released maps to NpcPresence.RETIRED, already terminal. Blocked on three prerequisites, each on another module: Actor.to_dict omits statuses, so a restored captive comes back with full health; an institution cannot hold a claim because SectState lives in the player's module_data (DEF-0119); and NpcPresence has no custody state. Recommend naming an NpcDef id and never an Actor, so the live actor is minted on demand.
next: Nothing. VERIFIED AND PINNED by commit 325c96528 with ADR 0263 (docs/adr/0263-a-captive-is-a-claim-and-a-term-is-a-count-neither-is-ever-priced.md). The code was already correct: game/tests/modules/custody/test_custody_captive_is_never_tradeable.gd asserts that after a capture no inventory item exists for the subject, MarketApi.list refuses it, EconomyValuation refuses to price it, and it can be neither dropped on the floor nor bought at a shop. CustodyState stores a subject DEF ID and an OwnerRef holder - never an Actor, an ItemInstance or a Resource. custody: 616 passed, 0 failed.

title: spine absorbed/overflow are inverted
reason: FIXED in game/src/modules/combat_engine/spine.gd: _absorb now TRANSLATES the component overflow return into the removed share, clampf(spendable - float(overflow), 0.0, spendable), so outcome.absorbed is what the shield took and outcome.overflow is what reached health. _spend is deliberately unchanged and is NOT where the fix belongs. THE PRESCRIBED FIX IS WRONG: swapping the two assignments in _spend does not work, because _absorb returned 0.0 for two different facts - no shield bound, and the shield took it all - so one number carried two opposite meanings and no arrangement of the two assignments is right for both cases. Measured by mutation on the combat_engine suite: the naive swap is WORSE at 600 passed / 27 failed than the pass-through at 601 passed / 26 failed, and it additionally breaks test_combat_immunity, which is a different defect; the shipped translation is 627 passed / 0 failed. The translation also closes an unbounded case where a hostile absorb returning more than it was handed drove overflow negative and spent the refund as a heal through the spine single sign flip. An absent shield now reads 0.0 for the only reason it should. The _absorb docblock records all of this and names DEF-0139. Also recorded as BL-0362.
next: Nothing further. The S9 translation inside _absorb is the whole fix and the spine.gd docblock names DEF-0139; the fix this entry prescribed is refuted by measurement above and must not be applied. See BL-0362 for the full five-defect diagnosis of this suite.

title: A transient core script corruption from a concurrent agent silently broke every test run, and the error was invisible
reason: core/breakthrough.gd line 297 held a truncated fragment 'y_advance(actor, path_id, condition, context)' left by an interrupted write. Because Breakthrough is depended on by body_cultivation, qi_cultivation and actor_factory, every tools test run failed at the import step with exit code 4294967295 and an EMPTY godot log - Godot crashed before it could report the parse error. Three orphaned test_zz*.gd.uid files from deleted probe scripts and a duplicated trailing line in ui/screens/loot_bridge.gd compounded it. Confirmed by running the suite directly with godot --headless -s res://tests/run_tests.gd, which bypasses the import pass and printed the real stderr.
next: REMEDY CORRECTED 2026-10-04. The next step said to run the engine directly: 'godot --headless --path game -s res://tests/run_tests.gd -- --suite <name>'. That is FORBIDDEN and must not be followed - INC-0004/0005: the RAM, log and clock ceilings live in tools/godot.py, so reaching for the binary gets NO ceiling at all, which is the exact shape behind the 73 GB resident run and the forced power-cycle. It is also unnecessary. tools test already carries the sanctioned flag: 'uv run python -m tools test --skip-import --suite <name>', which bypasses the crashing --import pass, keeps every ceiling, and still goes through the launcher. Verified live this session: three runs failed at the import step with 4294967295 and a 73-byte log, and --skip-import then produced a real result (625 passed, 9 failed) that named the failures. CORRECTED CAUSE: the 17 orphaned .uid files were removed and the crash persisted, so the named artefact is not the whole cause here - see BL-0783. Still true and still the rule: a crash with no log is an unreadable script, not a lock, so do not delete a lock and do not retry blindly.

title: PARRY_RATE and BLOCK_RATE modifiers are bucketed then discarded: no actor can parry or block
reason: actor_stats.gd _recompute calls _put only for the ids at lines 155-172. CombatStats.PARRY_RATE/BLOCK_RATE and the other parry/block/reflect/lifesteal ids are never _put, so their modifiers land in _buckets() and are then never read: a FLAT +1000 on parry.rate still resolves derived() == 0.0. Observed by headless probe, not inferred. Because p_parry/p_block are therefore always 0.0, the S2 band's parry and block branches are unreachable in every mode, which is why the 7 test_status_application gate failures never exercise their own gate. NOT status-owned.
next: CLOSED 2026-10-04 with ADR 0111. This entry's diagnosis was exactly right and the fix is at core/actor_stats.gd:187-189: every remaining modifier bucket is backed at 0.0 through the same _put formula after the core derived stats, so a FLAT on CombatStats.PARRY_RATE or BLOCK_RATE reads its own value instead of 0.0 and the band can actually enter its parry and block branches. test_combat_stats_shape went from 92 passed/12 failed to 104/0, mutation-proven by removing the backfill. The entry's open question - baseline _put or raw modifier sum - was answered as baseline _put, and that is why CombatStats.RATE_DEFAULTS stays all zeros (a PERCENT must not conjure a rate). The vacuous-gate consequence recorded in BL-0300 is closed with it.

title: Status system is a LIBRARY not a feature: no player action produces a status
reason: Re-verified 2026-10-04 by ADR truthfulness sweep. The shipped cleanse is unchanged and correct: StatusApi.cleanse(actor, lever) at game/src/modules/status/api.gd:293 refuses by name (no_actor, unknown_lever), matches an authored mitigation_tags, calls StatusRuntime.clear_modifiers and does NOT filter by scope; ItemDef.cleanse_lever at game/src/modules/items/item_def.gd:39; ItemUse._apply_consumed spends it through the real production verb at game/src/modules/items/item_use.gd:133-134; tests/modules/status/test_status_cleanse.gd passes 33/33. The ADR that now records it is docs/adr/0107-a-cleanse-verb-is-deferred-with-a-named-trigger-and-mitigation-tags-stays-the-vocabulary.md, whose amendment 'the trigger FIRED, and the verb shipped' carries the decision and the reasoning this row was duplicating. TWO numbers in this row are corrected by measurement and the ADR, not by this row alone: the trigger predicate is 238 pills carrying cleanse_lever TWICE, not once - consumable/cleansing_jade_pill.tres:16 and consumable/alchemy_clarity_pill.tres:23 are the only two of 7954 items that carry it - so ADR 0107's 'the first authored pill to name a lever' is false and the shipped count is 2; and the count of statuses a pill answers is 13, not fourteen. Twelve of the 20 defs in the authored catalogue (res://data/statuses, status_catalog.gd:31) publish pill, plus env_scourge (game/src/data/statuses/env_scourge.tres:26), which is a real StatusDef read by EnvironmentField.SCOURGE_DEF_PATH (environment_field.gd:286). ash_furnace.tres:14 also lists pill but is an EnvironmentZoneDef, not a status, and is not a fourteenth. The fourteen claim lives in a .tres comment (alchemy_clarity_pill.tres:17-20) that this wave is barred from editing, so it is reported in ADR 0107's Correction section rather than fixed here.
next: Nothing owed. tests/modules/status/test_status_cleanse.gd asserts the trigger predicate stays satisfied (33 passed), that a pill-tagged status is removed and a gear-only-tagged status survives, that one cleanse removes every matching status, that an unknown lever and a missing actor are refused by name, and that spending the authored pill through ItemUse.apply really does cleanse. Scope is deliberately unfiltered: a CULTIVATION blessing naming pill is removable by a pill, because filtering would show a player counterplay the game cannot deliver.

title: a custody term is a period count and a negotiated coin settlement, never a valuation
reason: ADR 0104's price decision, written ahead of the question. The module computes no price: it reads EconomyValuation only for numeraire_id, the unit of account. The transfer amount is agreed by the caller and zero is legal. Written now because the moment someone asks what a captured boss is worth, the tempting answer is to put RARITY_WEIGHT on a person, which would price a person off combat stats and make the 551x realm ladder into an economy money printer.
next: Nothing. VERIFIED AND PINNED by commit 325c96528 with ADR 0263. A custody term is {term_id, periods} and a count is arithmetic: game/tests/modules/custody/test_custody_term_is_never_a_valuation.gd asserts the row carries none of twelve valuation spellings (price, worth, value, valuation, base_worth, unit_price, coins, coin_value, amount, rate, rarity_weight and more) at every layer that persists it - capture, put, normalize, the world store, summary and a JSON save round trip - and that settlement moves an inventory-held curr_spirit_coin stack rather than setting a balance (ADR 0139). MUTATION-PROVEN BY ME, not merely asserted: making CustodyState.normalize pass an injected 'price' through turned the suite RED - 'price does not survive normalize: expected false, got true', Results: 184 passed, 1 failed - and reverting returned Results: 185 passed, 0 failed. The allowlist rebuilds every row key by key, so an injected price cannot survive a save. custody: 616 passed, 0 failed.

title: rebuild skips modifiers held by a binding whose pool the current realm tier no longer publishes
reason: api.gd:135-143 rebuild visits only the ids returned by equipped(tier), and technique_slots.gd:120-131 builds that list from the CURRENT tiers slot_keys. A binding taken at a higher tier (a universal slot before a demotion, or any pool whose count shrinks) is absent from the list, so its StatModifiers are never removed and stay on the actor permanently - the inverse of the suspension rule, which has an explicit clear path. _slots is never pruned for the same reason, so a stale binding also keeps occupying a key. This is latent only while tier never decreases, which is why 2934 passing assertions do not see it.
next: Make rebuild remove contributions for every id in the slot table rather than only those the current tier publishes, or make equipped() union the bound keys with the tier keys. Add a test that binds at a high tier, then rebuilds at a lower one and asserts the contribution is gone.

title: Slot bindings are never persisted, so a save and reload silently empties the whole loadout
reason: api.gd:54 constructs TechniqueSlots.new() with NO payload, while api.gd:52 passes actor.get_module_data(STATE_KEY) into the codex and api.gd:57 does the same for casting. title: quest now declares destiny in the registry; the arch gate was blind to the undeclared edge for its whole life
reason: Measured, not inferred. tools/arch/registry.json:161 gives quest deps [contracts, core], yet modules/quest calls the DestinyApi facade from five places: quest_grants.gd:62 (earn_fate), quest_grants.gd:67 (earn_destiny), api.gd:99, api.gd:124 and api.gd:276 (gate). The event module does this correctly - registry.json:79-88 lists destiny among event's deps - so the registry already knows how to record a module-to-module fate edge and the quest side is simply unrecorded. Why the gate does not catch it: tools/arch/rules.py:60 sets BARE_REF_UNITS = {ui, app, contracts}, which excludes modules/*, and rules.py:11-14 states the limitation outright - a bare reference out of modules/* is not a load-bearing edge the gate sees, and is only reported as an unresolved count. Confirmed empirically: tools arch reports 'ok boundaries ok (15795 files, 32 modules)' with the undeclared edge in place. The risk is not this one edge but the rule it breaks: an undeclared dependency is how a module cycle or an upward dep ships unnoticed, and quest is now a fate consumer whose boundary nobody has reviewed.
next: SHIPPED 2026-10-04. tools/arch/registry.json now lists destiny among quest deps, alongside combat, qi_cultivation, body_cultivation and mind_cultivation which declared it in the same cycle. The lesson is unchanged and now recorded in DEF-0237: a module-to-module edge is invisible to tools arch and to _find_cycle unless it is DECLARED, so an undeclared edge ships a cycle silently. If quest ever needs items to deliver the item grants it records as unspent, that is a second declaration, not a way around this one. Original note: add destiny to quest deps in tools/arch/registry.json, exactly as event already declares it. Do it as a one-line registry edit and re-run tools arch. If quest ever needs items to deliver the item grants it currently records as unspent (DEF-0107), that is a second declaration, not a way around this one. Longer term this is the AGENTS.md 0113-shaped lesson again: BARE_REF_UNITS excluding modules/* means every module-to-module edge is review-enforced, not gate-enforced, so a registry entry is the only durable record of it.

title: NpcApi.spawn returns a RefCounted Actor; WorldEntry.spawn_npc wants a Node2D
reason: Type-incompatible and unbridged. NpcApi.spawn (modules/npc/api.gd) mints an engine-agnostic Actor, which deliberately has no scene-tree presence (ADR 0001), while WorldEntry.spawn_npc (app/world_entry.gd) calls add_child on a Node2D. No scene extends WorldEntry today, so the two never meet -- but any future world scene with real npc markers cannot be stocked from the npc module without a bridge. A fake Node2D wrapper is NOT acceptable: it would mint a second identity no other system can see, so NpcRegistry, NpcApi.presence_here and WorldSpawn-derived interactable rows would all disagree about who is in the room. WorldStage.register_npc(actor) deliberately takes the Actor the caller already has instead of pretending to bridge.
next: Decide one: (a) a Body/Sprite2D view node owned by app/, registered with NpcRegistry as a presentation of an existing Actor, so one Actor has one identity and two representations; or (b) author real npc scenes and have ActorFactory return a Node-wrapped Actor. Whichever is chosen, it needs an ADR and a registry entry -- do not add an app/ -> npc import in the meantime.

title: EventApi.begin now has a production caller; EventApi.advance still does not, because no caller owns a PERIOD
reason:
Both halves are now closed, so the reason this entry was filed no longer holds. The
app-wiring agent authored the period owner this entry said did not exist:
app/world_pulse.gd:76 PERIOD_SECONDS := 120.0 is the single authored cadence, in
app/ because app/ is the only layer allowed to know real time. item_workbench_app.gd:117
pulls it on the same frame and same delta it already hands StatusLoop (the ADR 0106
convention), and world_pulse.gd:168 converts by arithmetic - int(_elapsed /
PERIOD_SECONDS), never a while - then hands the integer to EventApi.advance(actor,
periods). So EventApi.advance now HAS a production caller, which this entry recorded as
impossible.

Two claims in the old text are also wrong and must not be carried forward. The attach
is at item_workbench_app.gd:280, not :233 as written here - :233 is NpcBoot.install.
And "app/ is forbidden from inventing one" misreads the rule: app_state_warnings
(tools/arch/enforce.py:354) is a WARNING needing 2 of 3 signals, and an int period
counter carries none of them, so the period owner in app/ is permitted rather than
forbidden. An agent reading this entry would have concluded the opposite of what the
rule says.

Still open, and the real remaining gap: the event module records its own beat
(event/api.gd:561 -> EventBeatWriter.offer -> WorldFact.record) and never offers it to
the director, so EventBeatSink is registered and reachable but never consulted for an
authored event beat. Until that seam exists, ADR 0117's "recorded then resolved by one
director" is only half true, and re-recording through the director would double-count
because WorldFact.record is monotone.
next: Add an offer seam to the event module, following the NpcApi.set_minter inversion precedent: a static Callable injected from app/, used at event/api.gd:561, falling back to the module's own record when no offerer is set so the module's suites stay green. Then WorldPulse claims each beat exactly once and EventBeatSink stops being decorative. Second open gap, independent: no player-facing affordance calls advance_one_period() or reads world_summary(), so ui/ needs a route and a panel.

title: OPEN: the relation graph reads authored catalog only, so a PLAYER-driven event never reaches it - a declared schism and a declared war are both invisible
reason: modules/relations/relation_graph.gd:197-200 _payload() calls facade.summary(null) for every owner, so the graph is world-wide and reads only what the CATALOG publishes: dao factions from res://data/world/factions, and nothing else. But the two events that actually make institutions hostile at runtime are PLAYER-driven and live on an actor's module_data: SectApi.declare_schism writes sect_state['schisms'] (api.gd:685) and NationApi.declare_war writes the standoff. summary(null) returns {} for a null actor, so neither is ever visible to graph(), stance() or hostile_to(). The graph therefore answers the wrong question: it knows which AUTHORED factions disagree and nothing about what the institutions the player just split or went to war with actually think of each other. This is the same disclosed family as DEF-0119 (where a polity-wide ledger lives) - it is not a bug in the graph, it is the consequence of that ledger having no home yet.
next: Answer DEF-0119 first: decide where an institution ledger persists, then give the graph a way to enumerate those ledgers rather than reading one actor's. Do NOT special-case a schism by reading the caller's actor - that would make the graph world-wide in name and single-player in fact, which is worse than answering {} for a pair nobody has published. Until then the honest state is: the graph answers for authored dao stances only, and a declared split is a fact recorded in the sect's own ledger for a panel to read.

title: DESIGN QUESTION (human must rule): 2428 items claim a forager that does not exist - what is a gather supposed to MEAN, and may it be anything other than a forager module?
source: acquisition decision brief 2026-10-03, measured with tools data audit + tools data report + independent re-measurement (scratchpad/probe_edges.py)
reason: DEF-0169 records that gather is a MISSING SUBSYSTEM and hands a 3-step plan; this entry adds the question DEF-0169 does not ask, plus a corrected lever arithmetic that inverts its execution order. MEASURED (my own run, tools/data.py loaders, scratchpad/edges.txt): 7982 items, 1553 deliverable, 6429 blocked, signatures gather|quest 4150 / quest 1392 / gather 821 / unattributed 66. LEVER SIZES, both re-measured from scratch and both LARGER than the inherited figures: quest alone moves 1553 -> 7078 (+5525), gather alone moves 1553 -> 6591 (+5038), both -> 7981 (+6428; one item left, curr_spirit_coin, which declares no source at all). So quest is the BIGGER prize, not the cheaper half, and +1392 is only the quest-ONLY signature class, not the quest lever's edge: 3029 blocked items declare quest directly and the recipe closure carries the rest. THE UNRESOLVED QUESTION: holdings cannot be the forager - that is an ACCEPTED constraint, not a guess (BL-0191 status done; ADR 0097:59-65 "A node pays a ledger line, never items"; resource_node_def.gd:15-19; holdings/api.gd:21-24), pinned by two tests that state their own removal condition (tests/modules/holdings/test_holdings_yields_units_not_items.gd:26-32 and :218-231 forbid holdings/api.gd naming ItemsApi; tests/modules/quest/test_quest_cannot_deliver_an_item.gd:160-188 pins no_inventory_dependency). So a forager MUST be a new module. But nothing says what it may do, and the corpus does not agree with itself: of the 2428 gather items, 1174 are recipe inputs (forage as supply) and 373 are ALSO recipe outputs (forage duplicating craft), while the category census is material 1432 / consumable 268 / equipment 233 / technique 213 / misc 74 / currency 71 / key 70 / quest 67 - i.e. 487 of them are legendary equipment, techniques, CURRENCY and KEYS, which a forage action does not obviously hand out. The fiction cannot be read from the data either: ItemDef.description exists (item_def.gd:18) and is authored EMPTY on 0-of-7982 items, so no prose says a player picks these up. Also DEF-0174 is STALE: BeatDirector IS constructed at app/item_workbench_app.gd:77 and its QuestBeatHandler sink IS registered at app/world_pulse.gd:154, so the quest plumbing is more complete than DEF-0169 assumes and the quest option is cheaper than it looks.
next: Rule on the MEANING before anyone builds, because all four options cost real work and the meaning decides which is cheap: (a) FORAGE AS SUPPLY - a new forager module that yields only the 1174 recipe-input materials from placed nodes, leaving ~1250 non-input gather claims still unshipped; (b) FORAGE AS LOOT - a forager whose yield table is authored per node, which requires authoring node content (game/data/holdings/nodes/ does not exist) and deciding what a node may yield, since a node type carrying an item id is exactly what the holdings test forbids and a forager needs its OWN node type; (c) LET QUEST ABSORB THEM - strip gather from every item that also declares quest (4150 items) and author real QuestDefs, since quest is the bigger edge (+5525) and the quest module already ships; (d) RETIRE THE CLAIMS - delete or rewrite the gather source from the items no option above reaches. Whatever is chosen, the audit's numbers must move with it: flip KIND_GATHER shipped:false->true in item_sources.gd:89 AND add the matching RUNTIME_ROUTES entry in tools/data.py:246 in the SAME change, or _route_agreement_problems at tools/data.py:1089 fails. First concrete step for (b): author three node records under the NEW module's own data dir carrying the item ids they yield, and show one item actually arriving before the route is declared - the order named at tests/modules/holdings/test_holdings_yields_units_not_items.gd:26-32.

title: 6 of 17 authored fates had NO earn path and two quest gates were unsatisfiable cycles; partially repaired 2026-10-03
reason: SHIPPED; both halves of its next step are now satisfied and MEASURED. (1) THE WALKER: the reachability walk no longer refuses every `fact` verb as unreadable, which was why it could not see 4 of 8 authored events opening, and the hand-maintained KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_FATES allow-list - which certified two REACHABLE fates as permanently unearnable - is gone entirely. Measured: --suite destiny_reach is 37 passed / 0 failed. The two names it forgave (heaven_s_warning_unread, night_off_the_rotation) are both reachable in a normal run, traced by hand: the first through the_stone_that_answering.tres whose trigger is none_of[fact treasure_stone_read >= 1], true on a fresh ledger, and the second through auction_at_the_immortal_court.tres whose trigger is a bare has_fate first_blood_duel. (2) THE OWED AUDIT RULE: a `counter` gate naming an id with no COUNTER_FACTS row now FAILS the build - _counter_findings, whole-tree, with red AND green selftest cases - while an unproduced FACT stays a warning, because a gate closes a player door and a dormant row costs one dispatch.

The census remains honest and is deliberately NOT zero: `tools data audit` prints 3 COUNTER_FACTS rows naming a fact no shipped producer records (bound_name_called/severances, mountain_circled_once/heaven_marks, vigil_broken/watch_turned) and 1 FateDef.counters id with no row ('breakthroughs', declared by reborn_in_a_lesser_vessel and remembered_by_the_mountain). Those are WARNINGS and should stay warnings - a FateDef.counters declaration is read by no production code, so it declares documentation rather than a promise, and a gate can never name it until the row ships. Do NOT promote either to a failure without first wiring the owning module's producer, and do NOT add a counter gate on `breakthroughs` until a cultivation breakthrough writes that fact. The original row also required authoring a grant for whatever the walker still reported unreachable; it reports none, because the two it named were never unreachable.

title: WRONG-OPEN PREMISE: there is no building feature to wire rebirth into
reason: RESOLVED 2026-10-04. The audit was correct that no building feature existed - the search found zero gameplay hits and holdings has no build verb - and the rebuild did not try to make holdings into one. A new `anchor` module (ADR 0132) IS the building feature: a structure the player RAISES that repairs their soul while they stand in it. title: ADR 0099 says a numeraire is never held as an item; four modules hold it as one
reason: Unresolved contradiction between two accepted ADRs. ADR 0099 asserts the spirit coin is a unit of account held as an INTEGER ('purse(actor) -> int', 'not as an item in an inventory') and tools/data.py:161-163 enforces that by exempting subcategory=numeraire from the acquisition requirement and requiring it declare no sources. That premise is factually false about the code: economy/api.gd:142 reads it with inventory.count(), market/market_transfer.gd:64-66 reads it with inventory.has() and builds coin ROWS passed to EconomyExchange.exchange, market/api.gd:541 and custody/api.gd:201 do the same. So the coin IS a held stackable item and the exemption hides it from the acquisition graph: tools data audit now reports curr_spirit_coin as 'obtainable in the content graph but not through any shipping route'. One of the two must give. The fix is NOT to add a source to the coin - a unit of account should not be looted - it is to either (a) make the numeraire a real held item with a real earn route (gather or a domain drop), or (b) move the balance off Inventory entirely, which is a much larger change to EconomyExchange. Decision needed before the content wave, because the wave is what gives items worths and it must not give the coin one.
next: Nothing. RESOLVED by ADR 0139 (commit 2f843cd3), which superseded ADR 0099 on its own stated escape hatch. Measured rather than assumed: economy/market/custody all read the coin with inventory.count/has and pass coin ROWS into EconomyExchange, which physically removes and delivers the stack - so the coin is a held item and ADR 0099's exemption was hiding an unreachable item, which is exactly what data audit reported. Both exemptions removed from tools/data.py; the coin declares sources=[starter] and is in STARTER_ITEMS. starter and not gather deliberately: gather is graph-rooted but ItemSources.KINDS marks it shipped:false, so a gather source would have silenced the audit while leaving the coin unobtainable.

title: StatusCatalog leaks a probe id across suites, so the count is 21 not 20 in a full run
reason: FIXED and verified 2026-10-04. The leak had two halves and both are closed. (1) The leaking probe itself: game/tests/modules/status/test_status_refusals.gd:86 test_the_baseline_def_is_accepted_so_the_negatives_mean_something now registers through _tracked(_good(&"probe_accept")) instead of _good alone, so setup()'s _forget(probe_id) can erase it from StatusCatalog's _definitions, _ids AND _rejected - which is what removes the phantom 'claimed by fire_immolation, probe_also_claims_fire' entry as well as the 21st id. (2) A standing regression guard, which the entry never had: game/tests/modules/status/test_status_catalogue_pollution.gd asserts the process-wide invariant end to end - every PUBLISHED id is inside the authored CONTENT TREE (surplus == []), every AUTHORED id is published (absent == [], so a probe's cleanup cannot eat shipped content either), published.size() == authored.size(), and StatusCatalog.rejected() == []. The expected set is derived through the loader's own walk (ContentScan.files_under, the function StatusCatalog._scan delegates to) rather than a pinned twenty-id literal, so a future content addition does not make an honest guard go red. Its own probe is registered and cleaned. Verified: uv run python -m tools test --suite tests/modules/status --skip-import ends the run with the catalogue at exactly the authored twenty.
next: CLOSED. No further work. Both halves are asserted by standing tests rather than by a one-off measurement: the refusals suite can no longer leak a probe, and the pollution guard converts any future leaker of this shape from a silent 21-vs-20 into a named surplus id. Note for whoever next edits test_status_refusals.gd: any new probe registered against the StatusCatalog singleton MUST go through _tracked, or setup() cannot clean it and this guard fires.

title: Four of six criterion legs answer a bare false, so the observable clause of the acceptance gate was being read against a vocabulary they do not speak
source: Measured 2026-10-04 by a failure-branch audit (310 assertions) over all six legs; see BL-0680, BL-0682, BL-0683 and ADR 0150.
reason: The failure-branch audit measured that the {ok:false, reason:R} shape exists on only TWO of the six criterion legs. Train, break through, fail recoverably and reach-the-terminal-realm answer a bare false / {} / null. That is defensible on its own - a bool is a fine answer - but it means the ACCEPTANCE GATE clause "every failure branch reachable and observable" was being read against a vocabulary that four legs do not speak, so an audit that enumerated reasons would have found almost nothing and concluded the program was in good shape. The interesting refusals on those four legs are in the false, and they are the ones nobody can name. Proof was behavioural (typeof of each entry point is TYPE_BOOL while HeavenlyTribulationApi.begin returns a dictionary with ok and reason) and structural (comment-stripped source of the six entry points contains no "ok": false; tribulation_fight.gd does). Comment-stripping was load-bearing: heavenly_tribulation/api.gd documents the shape inside a docstring, so a raw grep reports a facade that authors no refusal as one that does - a false positive the audit caught and fixed.
next: Treat "observable" as unverified for four of six legs until ADR 0150 lands, and say so in any status report rather than quoting a refusal count. The audit also proved that on the tribulation leg four NAMED refusals sit behind disabled controls (tribulation_screen.gd:72-73), which is a different defect with its own decision: offer the control and explain, or publish the fact and stay disabled. Neither is right by default and ADR 0150 deliberately does not settle it. Worth adding to tools eventually: a check that a player-facing verb returning false has a name the screen can render - that is the guard whose absence let the seventh leg contradict itself with every suite green.

The body reachability suite now does both - setup deletes the real slot for a deterministic fresh boot, and a new test drives the restore branch on purpose - so copy that pattern rather than inventing one. title: ScreenStack.pop_to_root frees a screen while a Button.pressed from inside it is being dispatched
source: Measured 2026-10-04 by the agent that fixed the body element resistances; the locked-object error is reproducible via a real World Map click in the body panel.
reason: Found 2026-10-04 and reproducible in a real click, not a test artifact. game/src/ui/screens/screen_stack.gd:85 pops and frees a screen while a Button.pressed signal originating from inside that same screen is still being dispatched: body_cultivation_panel.act_world_map -> navigate_to -> pop_to_root. Godot reports 'Attempted to free a locked object (calling or emitting)' and the test that triggered it reports no assertion, so it shows up as an incomplete run rather than a failure. The obvious repairs are both blocked by existing rules: queue_free() is BANNED in res://src (tests/arch_rules/test_no_deferred_free.gd), because the headless runner drives every test from SceneTree._initialize() and a deferred free never runs there; and call_deferred does not run under that runner either. So this needs a real decision rather than a patch.
next: Decide the ownership rule and record it: who may free a screen that is mid-dispatch. The options are not equivalent. (a) The screen defers its own navigation until after the signal returns - but that needs a mechanism that works headless, which is exactly what call_deferred is not. (b) ScreenStack marks a screen as retiring and frees it on the next idle/frame boundary that the headless runner also reaches. (c) The button handler does not navigate directly; it asks the stack, and the stack decides when it is safe. (c) is the shape most likely to be correct because it puts the rule where the knowledge is, but it needs an ADR because it changes src/ui and src/app and interacts with the free()-not-queue_free rule's blast radius. Do not patch this without that decision - two obvious fixes are already ruled out.

title: QiAdvancement.cancel_attempt has no caller
reason: advancement.gd:32 is the only forwarder to QiBreakthroughTransaction.cancel -> _deviate, the one mechanism exercising voluntary deviation without a roll. Zero production and zero test callers, so the deviation path is unexercised.
next: RULED 2026-10-04 (session qi-wave4-design) - DELETED, not published. ADR 0180. The entry's suggested fix (publish cancel on both facades) was WRONG and re-deriving the code says why. Body and mind cancel a STORED attempt: BodyAdvancement._end (:289-296) and MindAdvancement._end (:482-489) both call committed.cancel() on a BodyAttempt/MindAttempt carrying trial_complete, and both document it as a REFUND - 'the pill stays spent and no deviation is owed: the trial never ran'. Qi has NO attempt to cancel: QiBreakthroughTransaction.execute (:92-168) validates, consumes the pill, rolls and resolves in ONE call, and no QiAttempt or trial_complete exists anywhere in the module. So qi's cancel was the semantic OPPOSITE of its siblings' under the same name - it called _deviate unconditionally, halving progress, scarring the dantian and burning a channel with no roll and no pill spent. Publishing it would have shipped a button that damages the player under a name meaning 'abandon safely'. _deviate keeps exactly one call site, the failed roll inside execute (:136-138), so failure reachability is unchanged and the involuntary path was never the question. GUARD: test_qi_ruling_q3_no_voluntary_deviation.gd asserts no cancel_attempt/cancel declaration, counts _deviate CALL SITES (a voluntary door is a second call site, not a verb), and separately proves a lost roll still deviates so deleting the voluntary verb did not delete the consequence. STILL OPEN, NOT MINE: mind's own unwired start/resolve/cancel (BL-0151) - mind DOES have a two-phase attempt, so publishing ITS cancel is a real fix there and was deliberately not touched.

title: A preloaded script const cannot hand out its instance members, so a shared test helper must be reached through an instance
reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 and the pattern is now GONE from the destiny tests: a findstr for script-const preloads of a Fixture or Probe across game/tests/modules/destiny and game/tests/arch_rules returns zero hits. test_destiny_earn_sources_cultivation.gd was the last holdout - it read `const BodyFixture := preload(...)` and then called BodyFixture.breakthrough / .actor / .prepare, which is a PARSE ERROR because a preloaded script constant exposes only that class's STATIC surface. It reported 'failed to load suite' and the tally UNDERCOUNTED every test in the file (0 passed / 1 failed, with all of them silently absent). It now holds one BodyPlayFixture instance reached through _body(), typed as the preloaded script so := still infers - a RefCounted return type erases the inference and the call sites fail again with 'Cannot infer the type of actor'. Measured: that suite is 80 passed / 0 failed.
next: SHIPPED for destiny. The general rule, now paid for twice in this file: a preloaded script CONST is only good for static members, so a shared GDScript test helper is either a class_name with static verbs or a preloaded script HELD AS AN INSTANCE - never a const read directly for members. DEF-0234 records the same lesson for the second occurrence. Two costs worth remembering, because they are why this is not a typo to fix later: the failure is a PARSE error, so the suite reports 'failed to load suite' and the tally UNDERSTATES rather than overstates; and a const initialiser reading through a shared instance would not have worked either, because run_tests.gd attaches a suite's properties one at a time so a const answers null during initialisation. To find any remaining instance of the pattern, grep for 'const' lines naming a Fixture or Probe, not for the method call.

title: A preloaded script const cannot hand out its instance members, so a shared test helper must be reached through an instance

title: The headless Godot engine is a single shared lock, so a filtered suite can be unmeasurable for hours while other agents hold it
reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 and the shape has CHANGED, which is why this entry needed correcting rather than just closing. It recorded the lock as a single named holder, so a run either waited or reported who held it. What actually happens now is a STORM: 80 concurrent Godot and python processes on one machine, and the observable symptom is a ZERO-BYTE output file rather than a message naming a holder. Measured three ways this round: a background run exited 0 with an empty file; a foreground run timed out at 600s with nothing written; and two of MY OWN runs deadlocked against each other, because --skip-import does not bypass the lock either. That last one is the new information: the lock is not only contended by other agents, it is contended by me.
next: Practical rules learned here, worth keeping because each cost a run: (1) NEVER launch two tools test runs concurrently yourself - they deadlock each other and you lose both; (2) a 0-byte output file means lock contention, NOT a passing run, so never read one as evidence; (3) a foreground run with a 600s timeout that writes nothing has told you what it is going to tell you, so kill it rather than re-issuing it, because a retry joins the storm; (4) scope the --suite filter as narrowly as the question allows, which is the only lever that actually reduces hold time. The durable fix is not in this row: it is thinning the concurrent agent count on the machine, which is an owner decision about how many sessions run at once, not something a deferral can fix.

What is now established: across a three-life ladder a hero carries up to 16 authored fate modifiers into every later body, so body 3 is strictly stronger than body 1 by authored amounts, with no authored curve for that and no answer for what the race ladder is now measured against. title: A null rng makes every body breakthrough roll the same number, and wiring the durable half makes it player-facing
source: Measured 2026-10-04; the rng_state degradation and the dead seed() sweep were confirmed by the agent that wired the durable half.
reason: Found 2026-10-04 by the agent that built the durable attempt affordance. A null rng degrades to rng_state = 0, which seeds _replay with 0, so every body breakthrough in the game rolls the same result. It was pre-existing and invisible while the one-press path was the only route; wiring the durable two-phase half makes it a shipped, player-facing roll. game/tests/modules/body_cultivation/test_body_cultivation_panel.gd:298 has a seed() sweep that does nothing for this reason, so the existing test cannot see it either.

Seed 0 is excluded by MASK, not by re-drawing - re-drawing until nonzero is an unbounded retry for a 1-in-2^31 condition, and a loop that may not terminate is a defect here. The defect was the OPPOSITE end of the distribution from first reported: a shipped body breakthrough could not FAIL. randf()=0.202272 against a lowest authored chance_base of 0.2580, so 'deviate when randf() >= chance' was false on all 30 realms and the whole deviation/recovery leg was unreachable in production. title: ItemWorkbenchPlay.npc_presence() has no player-visible consumer - no screen shows who is in the room
reason:
The read model is published and correct but nothing in game/src/ui/ reads it: grep for npc_presence across game/ returns exactly one hit, its own declaration at app/item_workbench_play.gd:262. So a probe or a test can see the settlement roster and a player cannot.

THE REASON WAS CORRECTED ON RE-VERIFICATION, because the first version of it was false. It claimed the repo has no screen whose content IS a room. That is wrong: game/src/ui/screens/domain_explore.tscn is exactly that, and it already renders the place you are standing in. The claim is withdrawn rather than defended.

WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS IT, measured: THE READ MODEL HAS NO CURRENT-ROOM KEY. npc_presence() returns a BOOT-TIME settlement - {spawned, location_id, npcs[]} captured once at NpcBoot.populate_room (app/item_workbench_body.gd:299, STARTING_CAST into &"mortal_plains") - and app/item_workbench_body.gd:175 states in code that this field is deliberately NOT restocked on a rebirth, because STARTING_CAST is a boot fact about the settlement the slice OPENS on, not a property of a body. So there is no 'where the player is now' state for a screen to key a roster on, and mounting one would mean the screen either lies (shows a stale boot cast as if it were the current room) or re-derives the room from NpcRegistry, which is precisely what app/item_workbench_play.gd:255-262 says not to do.

DomainExploreScreen does not already show this: its population comes from DomainApi.population(actor) (modules/domain/api.gd:173), which is the domain's SPAWN REFS - enemies and fixtures - not the named cast. Two different facts, so there is no double-draw to remove either.

Deferral, not silence: the reason and the trigger are written down so this is a decision and not an oversight. NOT blocked on anybody's ruling.

DONE 2026-10-05, in the two stages the deferral itself prescribed. STAGE 1 - the tracked current-room fact exists: `NpcBoot.where_is(actor)` reads `WorldSpawnApi.current(actor)`, the durable world_spawn ledger the world map writes when a player travels and the arrival path writes when a hero is born, and returns the place AND `presence_here` for that exact place in ONE read ({has_actor, location_id, display_name, located, here}). It keeps no second copy of the location, so it cannot drift from the module that owns it; it is deliberately not a `WorldFact` row, because moving rooms lowers one answer and raises another and a WorldFact is monotone (ADR 0065); and an unlocated hero is given `_no_room()` rather than `presence_here("")`, because the empty id means EVERYWHERE and that is the borrowed-neighbour defect wearing a location filter as a disguise. STAGE 2 - `NpcRosterPanel` ships, instanced by `domain_explore.tscn` as node `Roster`, with `show_room` as its ONE public mutator. The panel takes the tracked location verbatim and there is no `show_npcs`, no `cast` setter and nothing that accepts an array: a caller holding an array cannot check it belongs to the room on screen, so the stale-cast panel has no seam to be written through. `npc_presence()`'s boot settlement is deliberately NOT wired here. `ui/` may name neither `npc` nor `world_spawn` nor `app`, so `NpcRosterBridge` is the door and `NpcBoot.install` fills its `static var Callable` (the `NpcApi.set_minter` idiom) rather than a `_bind_route_screen` arm in a file another workstream owns; the install REFUSES a duplicate rather than being last-install-wins, the `WorldFact.subscribe` rule.
next: None. Re-measured green: game/tests/ui/test_npc_roster_panel.gd is the guard and it asserts the honesty rule by MOVING the hero rather than by inspecting a payload - it stocks mortal_plains through the production room-load verb, reads the panel, then moves the hero through WorldSpawnApi.selected into spirit_peaks and requires the panel to follow, the count to fall to zero and every name present before the move to be absent after it. A panel keyed on npc_presence() passes the first assertion and fails that one. The panel exposes exactly one public mutator (asserted off the SCRIPT's own get_script_method_list, since a Node has no such method), and the screen nests the panel's summary under `roster`. Sub-work: BL-0871 (the suite carried four expectations that contradicted the module's own contract - see its reason).

source: destiny program 2026-10-04, found while closing the ADR 0190 arrival-mark round
reason: RESOLVED, and an independent audit MEASURED the cause this row said was unmeasured. The guess recorded here (_earn returning true on a grant that added nothing) was wrong in its mechanism though right that _earn was the place. _fixpoint guards every node with `if held.has(tag(node_key)): continue` BEFORE calling _earn, so _earn is only ever entered for a node NOT in held - an already-held node cannot be the cause. The real mechanism is _earn's grants loop, which assigns `held[fate:<id>] = true` for each of node.grants WITHOUT checking whether the key was already present. Re-assigning an existing key is not an error and held.size() does not grow, so `changed` is set true, the outer while never sees an empty pass, and the loop runs to the cap. With ADR 0190's four arrival marks added as ungated sources there were enough duplicate-assignment nodes to push 64 to 65. Provenance: margins of 1, 2 and 3 moved the REPORTED count up in lockstep (28, 29, 30, 35), which is the signature of a cap that was never binding.
next: The fix is ONE line and it is NOT a cap change: make _earn report whether held actually grew (compare held.size() before and after the grants loop, or return false when every tag it wrote was already present). Then the walk terminates on its own condition at any cap. I did NOT make this edit - the audit that measured it was running under a do-not-mutate constraint and DEF-0271's own text said not to repair it silently. PROVE IT by asserting the shipped walk reaches a fixpoint in fewer than nodes.size() + 2 passes. See also DEF-0279: the same walker's KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_FATES allow-list certifies two REACHABLE fates as permanently unearnable, which is a test asserting a falsehood and is the more dangerous half of this file.

title: actor.gd:524 passes an int to set_module_data(data: Dictionary), and the parse error cascades to every suite in the repo
source: Measured 2026-10-04 from build/logs/233824-11288-1-run.log, whose error chain names the cause explicitly; both accused classes verified innocent under gdlint.
reason: Measured 2026-10-04 23:39. This ONE line is the root of the whole repo-wide cascade. game/src/core/actor.gd:524 calls actor.set_module_data(POLITY_SLOT_KEY, int(stamp_data)), but set_module_data is declared at actor.gd:266 as (id: StringName, data: Dictionary). Passing an int is a hard parse error, and the engine attributes it upward, so what you see is a lie about where the problem is: Could not resolve class LootContentTables, then Could not resolve class DomainFixtures 'because of a parser error' x4, then Failed to load script item_workbench_app.gd. LootContentTables and DomainFixtures are both innocent and both parse clean under gdlint. The design is correct and the CALL is wrong: POLITY_SLOT_KEY is a deliberately non-Dictionary version stamp, its own docblock at :513 says 'a NEW payload carries an int, which is copied straight back', and lines 391-393 and 410 already write it straight into module_data without going through set_module_data. So line 524 should write module_data[POLITY_SLOT_KEY] the way its siblings do, not route an int through a Dictionary-typed setter.
next: One line: write module_data[POLITY_SLOT_KEY] = int(stamp_data) directly, matching :393 and :410. It sits in game/src/core/actor.gd, which had 84 uncommitted insertions and an mtime 47s old when measured, so INC-0041 forbids an outside edit - the session that wrote it owns the fix and will see the loud parse error in its own next run. This is a TYPE fix that restores the documented intent, not a core behaviour change, so it needs no ADR; if the peer instead decides the stamp SHOULD be a Dictionary, that IS a behaviour change to a save payload and needs one. Do not 'fix' it by loosening set_module_data's signature - the Dictionary type is what keeps every other module_data slot honest.

title: claim_floor is unreachable: _meets_floor reads standing an OwnerRef never carries
reason: Found while building the player-reachable forage surface. HoldingsApi._meets_floor (holdings/api.gd:388) compares the node's authored claim_floor against the OWNER REF's 'standing' field. A plain {kind, id} OwnerRef - which is what ForageScreen._owner() and ForageAction.owner_ref() both build - carries no standing, so it reads 0 and every node authored with claim_floor > 0 refuses 'claim_below_floor' for a player forever. 7 of the 16 authored nodes have claim_floor > 0, so nearly half the resource content is permanently unclaimable and no suite caught it because the tests' fixtures all used floor-0 nodes. Two honest fixes, both a design decision: (a) an OwnerRef gains an optional standing field the resolver fills, or (b) the floor is read from the institution's claim rather than a bare ref. Not taken unilaterally because it changes a ref's shape in contracts/.
next: Nothing. RESOLVED by ADR 0248: claim_floor now counts the resource nodes the holder ALREADY holds, a concentration gate read entirely from this module's own ledger. It read owner.get('standing') before, which is always 0 because an OwnerRef is {kind, id} and both production producers build exactly that - so 7 of 16 authored nodes refused claim_below_floor forever and no suite caught it because every fixture used a floor-0 node. The old rule also refused every non-actor holder outright, so an institution could never take a floored node; a count is a fact for all four OwnerRef.KINDS and is keyed by storage_key so a clan and an actor sharing an id cannot answer each other's floor. holdings: 258 passed, 0 failed across 4 suites.
