title: The span guard's SELF_EXEMPT was untyped and silently did nothing, so the guard scanned 1258 assertions instead of 8351 and reported itself
source: 2026-10-04, found while verifying the guard I had just repaired
reason: MEASURED, and it is the second half of the compile failure I fixed in DEF-0279's sibling. test_no_unbounded_wait.gd declares `const SELF_EXEMPT := [...]` UNTYPELED while `_bound_is_exempt(bound: String, exempt: Array[String])` is typed, so every call raised a RUNTIME error - 'Invalid type in function _bound_is_exempt. Typing the constant (`const SELF_EXEMPT: Array[String] = [...]`) makes the exemption work, and the same suite immediately jumps to 8351 passed - the guard was inspecting roughly one assertion in seven. A loop-safety guard that cannot exempt itself is a guard that reports itself, which is how a guard gets muted.

title: test_the_qi_facade_entry_point_earns_too is a COIN FLIP - QiCultivationApi.attempt_breakthrough takes no rng, so the roll is random and the test's found seed is never used
source: 2026-10-04, found by bisecting a cross-suite failure rather than by a red run
reason: SHIPPED 2026-10-04 (commit e5cccd1e7). Confirmed by measurement, not inference: the case computed rng := _qi_roll(hero, true) - a seed searched over 1..SEED_CAP for a WINNING outcome - then called QiCultivationApi.attempt_breakthrough(hero) and never passed it. The facade signature is attempt_breakthrough(actor: Actor) -> bool handing QiBreakthroughTransaction.execute(actor, null), so the transaction drew its own roll and the searched seed was used for NOTHING. Evidence it was a coin flip: the suite read 80 passed / 0 failed ALONE and 2 failed when run immediately after test_destiny_earn_sources_combat, same code and same tree - a different random draw. A green run of the file therefore proved nothing about the thing it names. The roll is now retried within the same SEED_CAP bound the rest of the file uses, so a breakthrough that never succeeds in 256 attempts is a real finding rather than a flake, and the claim the case exists to make - the UI's Breakthrough button is not a walk past the earn - is kept and is finally worth something.
next: SHIPPED for the test. STILL OWED in production, and this row is the evidence for it: QiCultivationApi.attempt_breakthrough has NO rng parameter, so the facade is the ONLY lossy hop - QiBreakthroughTransaction.execute already takes one, and QiAdvancement.try_breakthrough already accepts one, so the seed can be threaded everywhere except through the facade. Adding the parameter would be a 13th facade method and fail tools arch at the 12 cap (ADR 0134), so the honest fix is a deterministic seed SOURCE on the transaction rather than another verb. Until then this case retries, which is correct but slower than a seeded assertion - and a reader should know the retry exists BECAUSE the facade cannot be seeded, not because the test is flaky. Two things the runner caught that reading did not: the source constant is QiAdvancement.EARN_SOURCE and not QiCultivationApi.EARN_SOURCE, and an interrupted pass had left a docstring mid-sentence at the case's head, which was repaired rather than deleted because it is the only prose explaining why the facade is a separate earn site.

title: test_destiny_earn_sources_combat fails 3 cases on the CombatExchange entry path, which no longer enters a domain
source: 2026-10-04, the last 3 failures in the destiny suite at 1872 passed / 3 failed
reason: SHIPPED 2026-10-04. My first diagnosis was WRONG and this row records the correction, because the wrong diagnosis is the more useful half. I claimed the three cases failed at the SETUP - 'LootApi.enter_domain no longer enters a domain' - and that was inference from a failure MESSAGE rather than a measurement. Re-running the suite alone showed '_entered' PASSES and the duel is decided ('the duel was decided: a blow landed and the defender did not get up' is green); only the three EARN assertions failed. So the fight worked and the reward did not, which is the opposite shape. Traced to the real cause: CombatDuelHit._record_win (duel_hit.gd:237) called CombatDuel.record_win(duel, entry) WITHOUT the third argument, and record_win's signature is (duel: Dictionary, entry: Dictionary, actor: Actor = null) with `if actor != null:` guarding the earn. The default therefore took the branch that SKIPS the earn entirely: a duel closed with a killing blow moved the `wins` counter, wrote `duel_won` into the duel history, recorded the duel fact, and granted NO fate. Pure UNWIRED - the site existed, typechecked, read as correct, and paid nothing.
next: SHIPPED: _record_win now passes `attacker`, so a killing blow earns first_blood_duel and verifies it. Measured --suite earn_sources_combat at 49 passed / 0 failed, from 46/3. The transferable lesson, which is the signature's: AN EARN SITE WHOSE PARTICIPANT IS A DEFAULTED PARAMETER IS A SITE THAT CAN WIRE TO NOTHING AND STILL TYPECHECK. record_defeat's caller passed its actor and DEF-0105's earn was verified there, so the win was the only one of the two that did not - which is why the defect was invisible to a census that counted `DestinyApi.earn_fate` CALL SITES and found twelve. Counting sites proves a call exists, never that it is REACHED. The stronger guard, owed and not yet written: an earn site whose participant can be null should not compile - either make the parameter required, or have the census assert that every earn call sits on a path where its participant is non-null. Do not simply drop the default without checking the other callers.

title: A base-attribute GRANT needs no new verb; only a paired TRANSFER does, and nothing in the tree removes from a base stat
source: doctrine program slice 7 investigation, corrected 2026-10-05 after re-measuring
reason: Measured, then CORRECTED after re-reading the apply path. set_base is called from 11 sites across 5 modules and EVERY one is an addition: qi_cultivation/training.gd:178, qi_cultivation/breakthrough_transaction.gd:152, mind_cultivation/training.gd:158, mind_cultivation/advancement.gd:506, body_cultivation/advancement.gd:334, body_cultivation/progress.gd:44, body_cultivation/training.gd:43, body_cultivation/weapon_demand.gd:86+95, race/race_projection.gd:138+156, items/item_use.gd:184, core/tribulation.gd:389+404+419. Not one subtracts, so the GRANT half needs no new verb and only a TRANSFER is a real gap. The mechanism is where I was wrong first time: I wrote 'sell a bound, realm-gated CONSUMABLE', and item_use.gd:136-140 says the opposite in as many words - a consumable whose only content is a base attribute 'restores nothing and applies nothing' under ADR 0001, its stat_gains are REPORTED in the payload and never applied, and REASON_NO_EFFECT refuses it. The permanent grant lives in _apply_LEARNED (item_use.gd:176-186), which does set_base then mark_stats_dirty. So there are two shipped paths and they are not interchangeable: a permanent base-attribute grant needs a LEARNED item, a transient one needs a consumable through Actor.add_status.

When a candidate actually needs re-specification the decision owed is: which module owns it, given ItemsApi is the god facade at fan-in 11 and the new MAX_FACADE_FAN_IN guard warns on exactly that shape; whether the two attributes move as a PAIR or the cost is charged separately; and what bounds a transfer so it cannot become a realm-scaling power curve in disguise (a rate must never track a magnitude, ADR 0050). option_catalog is a value and bounds authority, not a writer - make_effect normalises a record and clamp_to_bounds bounds a number, neither touches an actor - so it supplies the shape but not the commit.

title: world_id on SaveSlot: the world an actor was born into is not recorded, so a save cannot be filed under one
source: ADR 0271 decision 4 (organizations stay world-scoped; world_id addressing deferred)
reason: ADR 0261 is PROPOSED, not Accepted, and SaveSlot has NO world_id field today - measured: rg 'world_id' game/src/modules/save/save_slot.gd returns nothing. Addressing a world before the field exists would be a second guess at a field ADR 0261 still owns, and the world key the ledger already rides (world.polity) is an ENVELOPE key, not a world identity. WorldPolityLedger is world-scoped in the sense that it lives on the save ENVELOPE beside the actor, which is what DEF-0119 decided; that is not the same as being filed under a named world.
next: Blocked on ADR 0261 being Accepted. When it is: add world_id to SaveSlot, have app/world_ledger_store.gd route the world key by it (the routing-by-container-NAME precedent is already there), and then the two rows below become reachable. Do not add a world_id to an institution ROW before SaveSlot has one - a row addressing a world nothing can name is a second identity, which is the ADR 0066 failure mode.

title: world_id on WorldPolityLedger.institutions rows: an institution is not filed under the world it was founded in
reason: Depends on DEF-0323 (world_id on SaveSlot). The ledger's containers are [institutions, debts] keyed by a BARE institution id, and the envelope slot is world.polity, so two worlds sharing one process have no way to hold a same-named institution apart. The debt half is already unambiguous because pair_key is derived from two ids and both sides must be named - it is the SINGLE-institution row that is ambiguous.
next: Only after DEF-0323 lands and ADR 0261 is Accepted. Then either scope the row key as world_id|institution_id, or give the ledger a world_id and assert every row's world matches on normalize. Whichever is chosen, WorldPolityLedger.normalize_payload must FOLD two rows naming one institution in different worlds rather than overwrite one - the pair-fold mechanism already there is the precedent.

title: A module's dependency list exists twice with no gate: tools/arch/registry.json and module_registry.gd's BASE_DEPS mirror

title: No list of valid resource ids exists anywhere, so a pool id that is a typo of ANOTHER System's id still reads 0.0
reason: Narrowed by slice 6, not closed. DoctrineRegistry.attach now fails loudly on an empty id, a duplicate, an ActorPools.CORE_POOL_STATS id, a row spending a pool it did not declare, a priced row naming no pool, and a declared pool no row spends - six real closures. title: doctrine (a System own transmitted rules) and SectDoctrineDef (a school teaching) are different concepts sharing one word
reason: Both concepts are in the tree and both are called doctrine. SectDoctrineDef is a sect institutional teaching (BL-0186): what a school holds and what membership confers. DoctrineApi and DoctrineRule are a registrable System: the rules a practitioner holds for themselves, which grant values and rates and carry no institutional recognition at all. They are close in wording and far in meaning, so conflating them is a design error rather than a typo: one is granted by joining an institution, the other is bought with a System own currency and has nothing to do with sect membership. ADR 0273 records why the module is named doctrine (system collides with engine vocabulary) but does not acknowledge the word was already taken in this codebase by an unrelated concept.
next: No rename is owed: both names are accurate for what they are, and renaming sect vocabulary would touch an unrelated module public surface for a reader benefit. What is owed is one sentence in either ADR 0273 or the sect documentation stating the two are unrelated, so the next agent who meets both does not spend a turn trying to reconcile them. Whichever file is edited, verify git status --short on it first: sect is actively held by sect-duty-def0196.

title: The doctrine framework ships 3 verbs with no production caller by design, and no allowlist reason distinguishes that from a real defect
reason: Measured with no_caller_verbs --modules doctrine: rules, boards and redeem have zero production callers. That is not an oversight and it is not DEF-0303's shape - DEF-0303 deleted technique_state because nothing reached it by accident, whereas these are the framework's entire reason for existing. The program ships the seams and NO System (ADR 0273), so by construction nothing in production calls a System-shaped surface until the first System is authored. The default guard scope is quest and event only, deliberately and with a documented reason (no_caller_verbs.py:84-96, ADR 0188 applied-per-member-not-in-bulk), so tools arch does not grade doctrine today and the tree is green. The hazard is later: the scope is meant to widen, at which point these three are indistinguishable from the 103 real caller-less verbs the same sweep reports, and redeem - the one verb that makes a doctrine a two-sided mechanic - is deleted as collateral.
next: When the scope widens past quest and event, give these three an entry in tools/arch/no_caller_allowlist.json with a reason that says WHY, in the words the allowlist already requires: no System ships yet, the verb is the framework surface, and it must not be deleted before one does. Do not widen the scope to include doctrine as a way of testing the allowlist - that turns a deliberate scope note into 3 reds. Check git status --short on tools/arch/no_caller_allowlist.json first: it is shared and its stale-entry check is already failing on other entries.

title: Twelve mind stat ids are registered in Stat.RATE_STATS with no baseline anywhere in res://src, so two contract guards fail

title: A mod cannot run load-time code: an attach hook receives only the actor, and no entry-point seam exists
source: doctrine program slices 5 and 8, independently reported 2026-10-06; re-filed same day after a revert
reason: RE-FILED after a path-wide revert destroyed the original entry. Measured, and it is the gap the doctrine template had to work around rather than a missing convenience. game/src/app/attach_pipeline.gd fires every hook as callable.call(actor), so an attach hook structurally CANNOT receive the RegistrationContext - it has no parameter for one. And there is no entry-point seam anywhere in game/src/modules/mods: a search for entry_point across all of game/src returns only world_entry.gd unrelated world-map markers. So a mod has exactly two hooks - register_module at load, attach(actor) per actor - and neither can run once-at-load logic. The doctrine template needs exactly that: registering a System means calling DoctrineApi.attach(rule), which is neither registering a module nor attaching an actor, so its test drives boot(ctx) DIRECTLY and no production path calls it. Slice 5 hit the mirror from the other side: it wanted the declaration block read on the boot path, noted a separate read step the composition root would call would have NO caller, and put the read inside ModRuntime.finalize where every boot passes.
next: The decision owed is whether load-time code is a seam at all. If it is, it is a SEVENTH and amends ADR 0184 decision 6 again - which already took a sixth for the declaration block in ADR 0275 - so it needs its own ADR and cannot be smuggled in by widening RegistrationContext. If it is not, the template mod is honest to have no boot(ctx) and the framework should document per-actor attach as the only hook, which makes a System registry reachable only from app wiring. Either answer is defensible; leaving it unstated is not, because a mod author will write boot(ctx), see it pass its own test, and ship a System that never loads. Check git status on game/src/app/attach_pipeline.gd and game/src/modules/mods/ first, both are contended.

title: The Python gate _valid_stats accepts the stat id slow, which exists only inside a docstring, so it disagrees with the GDScript loader
source: doctrine program verification, 2026-10-06, probe under build/; re-filed same day after a revert
reason: RE-FILED after a path-wide revert destroyed the original entry. MEASURED with a probe, not reasoned. _valid_stats in tools/data.py learns stat ids by regexing an ampersand-quoted lowercase word out of contracts/stat.gd, on the stated intent that the audit follows the real schema. That regex also matches inside DOCSTRINGS, and stat.gd contains MindVocabulary.offence_id with the word slow in prose, so slow is returned as a valid stat id. The probe returned 62 ids with slow accepted, and proved the regex is not matching arbitrary text: the controls the, ids, generated and mindcontrol are all correctly refused, and the other five mind suffixes cost, falsify, invert, voice, intent are correctly refused too. So this is ONE tight false accept, not a broken parser. It matters because _resolve_rate_stats own docstring states these ids are BUILT from a prefix and a suffix so no const exists to match - the function that understands that has a fallback and the function that validates mod declarations does not. A mod declaring a stat named slow therefore passes the Python audit while the GDScript declaration reader, one id stricter, refuses it. Two gates disagreeing on the same id is exactly the failure BL-0767 names.
next: Do not fix _valid_stats by loosening or removing the regex: the GDScript loader is already the stricter and correct side, so the cheap repair is to make the Python gate read the same derivation - the declared const table plus the generator calls, the way _resolve_rate_stats already falls back to them - rather than scanning a file that contains prose about its own contents. A narrower stopgap is to strip docstring and comment lines before the regex, which closes this instance and leaves the general shape. BL-0767 is the same disagreement from the unit-trust side; close them together or sequence them explicitly. Check git status on tools/data.py first - a session holds it.

title: adr-cite fails 595 of 1033 citations tree-wide, and 356 of the 367 unresolved are written forms its resolver cannot pin to a file
source: doctrine program verification sweep, 2026-10-06, probe under build/; re-filed same day after a revert
reason: RE-FILED after a path-wide revert destroyed the original entry. MEASURED with a probe against a full adr-cite --json sweep, not estimated. Tree-wide counts: 367 unresolved, 228 symbol_miss, 266 unchecked, 168 ok, 2 waived, 2 line_past_eof - so 595 of 1033 citations FAIL on a tree where almost nothing is actually wrong. The breakdown is what matters and it is not what the verdict suggests. adr_cite.Resolver.resolve collapses three distinct situations into the single verdict unresolved, and the detail field separates them: 216 are a BARE FILENAME with no directory, where the tree simply holds six files named advancement.gd so the basename index is ambiguous; 140 are a LINE RANGE such as test_arch_rules.gd:473-483, which is not a single line the tool can read; 4 are duplicate-path ambiguities. That is 356 of 367 - ninety-seven percent - written in a form the resolver cannot pin, and only SEVEN citations name a file that genuinely does not exist. The other bucket is more real: 138 of 228 symbol_miss are the plus-or-minus-3 tolerance window, meaning the cited line genuinely moved, and 90 name several symbols where none sits at the line.
next: The cheap fix is in the resolver, not in 356 ADRs. A bare filename is ambiguous only because the resolver gives up on the path; it already holds the named symbol, so it could search every candidate file for that symbol and accept the one carrying it, turning 216 failures into resolutions. A line range could resolve against any line inside it rather than requiring a single integer. Do not do either by loosening the check until it passes - that is the move this repo already made once with a threshold, and it made the guard trusted on day one by reporting nothing. After the resolver change, re-measure: genuine drift should become visible, which today it is not, because 356 unresolvable citations bury the 138 real ones. Nobody should be asked to fix 595 findings when 7 of them are real.

title: mutation_history reads refs/remotes/*, so tools check is red for work that is committed but not pushed
source: corrected 2026-10-06, minutes after filing, on reading the tool's own shipped_refs rationale
reason: CORRECTED IMMEDIATELY AFTER WRITING IT - the original recommended weakening a guard that is right. The tool is deliberate: shipped_refs() ALLOWLISTS refs/heads/ AND refs/remotes/, and its own comment says those are the refs that ARE the repository, for everyone, on every machine - as opposed to refs/stash and the agent-local namespaces a harness leaves behind. That choice is sound: a probe that reached origin/main HAS shipped to every colleague, which is exactly what the guard exists to catch, and an allowlist rather than a denylist means a new agent namespace cannot silently narrow it. So the report is CORRECT, not a false positive. What I misread as a mis-tuned gate is a true finding about a tree that is behind: refs/heads/main is clean - the probe is gone from local main and from HEAD - while origin/main and origin/HEAD still carry it because the deletion is committed and unpushed, local HEAD being 5 commits ahead. The gate is reporting push state accurately.

The entry's own correction stands: shipped_refs is deliberately an allowlist of refs/heads and refs/remotes, so nothing was owed in the tool; the red was push state and it has cleared.

title: A guild cannot project recognition: the allowlist has no field on InstitutionPositionDef and its only consumer is SectProjection, inside sect
reason: DONE in core, with the CONSUMER and the field in one change - which is what the earlier slice required and why it refused the field alone. (a) core/institution_position_def.gd now carries @export var standing_percent_stats and its 'deliberately absent' bullet is replaced; the class note records that the VALUES are never read and only the KEYS are content. (b) core/institution_projection.gd (new) is the shared consumer, a pure function of (allowlist, standing, source_tag, actor) naming no module and no clock. VERIFIED the prior slice's measurement that SectProjection._grant's loop is a pure function of those four: its only sect coupling is the catalog lookup and two envelope keys, neither of which moved. (c) The two owed tests now run ON THE NEW CLASS: realm-invariance in RATIO and strip-then-rebuild idempotence, plus a guild member's stat moving and moving AGAIN on demotion. (d) MEASURED, and it CONTRADICTS part (c): the loop is NOT safe to delegate unchanged, because writing without stripping compounds - five rebuilds climbed the modifier stack 2,4,6,8,10,12 while every sheet assertion still read plausibly. grant now strips its own tag, and the validation runs BEFORE the strip so a refusal is non-destructive (ADR 0083's third state writes nothing, ADR 0044). (e) SectPositionDef.recognises is SUPERSEDED, not carried: it has zero callers and the read is now InstitutionProjection.recognises, so deletion is correct - sect was not in this slice's claim, so the change is reported rather than made. (f) The shape test ADR 0084 asks for CANNOT be written in tools arch, and it is not decidable at runtime either: an id the sheet cannot NAME is a static fault (unknown_stat refuses it by name), while an id that merely reads zero on a member who invested nothing is an ordinary sheet. So the content half is a test over every id the shipped .tres files name, measured on an actor invested in every attribute - the only sheet on which the two separate - and its RED path is asserted in the same breath against Stat.DAMAGE_REDUCTION, the id ADR 0068 documents as deriving a literal 0.0. (g) NationOfficeDef is a THIRD copy of the field, so the sweep covers sect AND nation; a sect-only sweep would have reported 'every shipped allowlist' while measuring half of them.

title: The mind contest's steepness band (steepness < 0.25) has no load-time gate, and four control defs sit outside it
reason: The suite documents the design: a def whose steepness >= NEUTRAL/2 = 0.25 has p_land = NEUTRAL + edge*steepness pinned at or below 0.5 for every defence, so its refusal rate can never leave [floor, floor + headroom*0.5] and a saturating attacker never reaches the authored floor. The suite's guard computes the clamp ratio (NEUTRAL+s)/(NEUTRAL-s) and demands it <= OUT_INVESTING 3.0 (s <= 0.25); mind_status_def.problems() enforces NO steepness bound at all. Four shipped control defs violate it: mind_unmake 0.28, mind_hush 0.30, mind_falsify 0.32, mind_daze 0.35 (ratios 3.545 / 4.0 / 4.556 / 5.667). Measured consequence: at a saturating attacker (OVERPOWERED vs WEAK) the refusal rate is floor + headroom*(NEUTRAL - steepness) -- mind_hush reads 0.67 where its authored floor is 0.60 -- so the saturated reading is not the bare floor the suite asserts; 126 failures across the four defs and both checks. The refusal sits ABOVE the floor, so this is a design-conformance break rather than a lock risk, and the suite's other hard properties (no certainty, monotone direction) pass.
next: Owner ruling needed: either author the steepness gate in MindStatusDef.problems() and re-band the four defs below 0.25 (one guard + content, no contest rebuild), or re-derive the contest form so a saturated attacker reaches the floor across the whole band and update the suite's two checks. Until the ruling the suite stays RED as the live evidence (658/126); T14 cites this entry.
